approachQuestion.prompt:
Distribute a Chain Across Folders

A finite acyclic singly linked list has n record nodes. Given positive integer k, cut it into exactly k consecutive parts, preserving every node, value and order. Part lengths differ by at most one and are nonincreasing from left to right. Return an array of k head references, using null for empty parts; each nonempty part must end in null. Change only next links. Input is head and k, not n. Constraints: 0 <= n <= 200000; 1 <= k <= 200000.

Input: [1,2,3,4,5,6,7], k=3. Output heads for [1,2,3], [4,5], [6,7].
Input: [8,9], k=4. Output heads for [8], [9], null, null.

Choose a method that satisfies the full contract with the best worst-case running time, breaking time ties by least auxiliary storage.

options.text: Put q nodes in each part and put every remaining node into the last part.
options.feedback: For n=7,k=3 this gives sizes 2,2,3, violating nonincreasing lengths; n=8,k=3 gives 2,2,4, also violating balance.

options.text: Calculate the balanced head positions and return them without changing next links.
options.feedback: For [1,2] and k=2 the first returned head still reaches both nodes, so the first part is not a one-node null-terminated list.

options.text: Count n. Let q be n divided by k and r its remainder. Allocate the k-reference output array. For part indices below r take q+1 nodes; for the rest take q nodes. Record each head and cut its tail, or write null for length zero.
options.feedback: The quotient and remainder give the only nonincreasing balanced sizes; cutting each tail makes the parts independent.

options.text: Collect all nodes into a temporary array, derive the same q/r lengths, and use indexed boundary nodes to fill the k-reference output and cut the links.
options.feedback: The boundaries are correct, but the temporary node array adds avoidable storage beyond the returned head array.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (acm-b15-18-target), regardless of your Q1 choice. Here n is the input length and k is the required number of returned entries. Choose the tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Count each node allocation, link access, identity/value comparison and machine-word operation as constant work. Include all temporary collections and call frames; exclude supplied nodes and the final returned output only. Copying or allocating k records costs k operations. No hash-table, amortized-operation or tail-call assumptions are used.

options.explanation: This pair does not describe the fixed method. Counting and cutting traverse linear total input nodes, and writing all k output entries costs k operations even when n=0. Only fixed counters and traversal references are auxiliary. The k-reference result array is output, excluded from auxiliary storage, but its allocation/initialization is included in time.
